## Fiscal 27 Q1 Aide Memoire


**Fiscal 27 Q1 Aide Memoire**


This document sets out public information previously provided by Diageo plc, or else widely available in the market. Unless otherwise specified, the outlook comments below come from the fiscal 26 FY results materials and Capital Markets Day (CMD) presentations, with other content sourced from publicly available information. No new information is given. As usual there will be no comment on current trading or further guidance provided. Any updates to these and other previously made statements would only be included in further communications by Diageo to the market and the inclusion of the extracted statements herein should not be taken to indicate that they will not be updated in the future.


Please note that historic comparatives referred to in this document include the detail published in a separate release on Regional Restatement for fiscals 25 and 26 issued this morning. This change does not impact overall group numbers.


**Fiscal 27 outlook**


With the fiscal 26 FY results and CMD on 6 August 2026, we provided the following guidance for fiscal 27:


- **Organic net sales growth** – broadly flat organic net sales growth. North America organic net sales expected to decline mid-single digit **** assuming the market is down c.3% with improving share performance compared to fiscal 26.
- **Organic operating profit** – up low-to mid-single digit. This includes c.40% of the c.$850 million cost savings from the operating framework changes and c.25% of the supply chain savings of c.$150 million.
- **Taxation** – expect tax rate before exceptional items to be c.25% (F26: 24.3%).
- **Effective interest rate** – **** expect effective interest rate to be c.4% (F26: 3.9%).
- **Capital expenditure** – of c.$1.25 billion (F26: $1.2 billion). ****
- **Free cash flow** – c.$2 billion (F26: $3.2bn) after c.$850 million exceptional costs related to operating framework changes and the supply chain savings programme.


**Overall net sales performance comments** ****


Fiscal 26 FY organic net sales declined 2.0%, with volume down 0.4% and price/mix down 1.6%. Negative price/mix largely reflected weakness in US Spirits and Chinese White Spirits (CWS). In Q1 F26, organic net sales were flat, with volume up 2.9% fully offset by adverse price/mix. At the time we commented on solid growth in the quarter in Europe, LAC and Africa offset by weakness in CWS impacting Asia Pacific results and softer performance in North America given the decline in US Spirits.


**Geographic regions**


Please note regional numbers are presented on a restated basis, while market-level numbers have not been restated and are shown as originally reported.


- **North America -** In fiscal 26, organic net sales declined 8.5%, with volume down 7.0% and price/mix down 1.6%, US Spirits declined 11.5% reflecting softer spirits and competitive intensity. Diageo Beer Company USA organic net sales grew 4.4%. In fiscal 26 FY results we noted that overall distributor inventory levels were appropriate for the current consumer environment and in line with historical levels. In Q1 F26, organic net sales declined 2.7%. US Spirits declined 4.1% with tequila down double-digit impacted by comparatives, competitive pressure and category softness. Scotch saw strong growth, with Johnnie Walker up double-digit, and some favourable phasing from tariff-linked pull forward of European imports. On the Q1 F26 conference call Deirdre Mahlan, Interim CFO, said that the c.2.5% gap between shipments and depletions, with depletions lagging shipments, was not unusual for the time of year. DBC USA net sales grew 9.2% driven by Smirnoff Ice and Guinness.


- **Europe, Middle East & Africa** - In fiscal 26, organic net sales grew 5.9%, with volume up 5.2% and price/mix up 0.8%. In Q1 F26, organic net sales grew 4.9%, with volume up 3.1% and price/mix up 1.8%. ****


- **Asia Pacific -** In fiscal 26, organic net sales declined 12.0% primarily due to the 34.9% decline in CWS in Greater China. This was the result of market policy changes which impacted consumption occasions across the category. In Q1 F26, organic net sales declined 14.8%, driven by a strong double-digit decline in CWS. Additionally, the change in beer route-to-market in Australia and China adversely impacted performance.
- **Latin America & Caribbean –** organic sales grew 7.6% in fiscal 26, with volume up 2.7% and price/mix up 4.9%. Spirits grew mid-single-digit, led by scotch and vodka. RTDs and beer both grew double digit. In Q1 F26, organic net sales grew 10.9%, driven by double-digit growth in Brazil where Johnnie Walker and Smirnoff Ice RTDs performed strongly. Mexico was broadly flat, with mid-single-digit volume growth mostly offset by negative price/mix as the consumer environment continued to stabilise.
- **India –** organic net sales grew 7.1% in fiscal 26, driven by positive price/mix and strong scotch led by Johnnie Walker and Black & White. Smirnoff saw strong double-digit growth with local flavour innovations. Maharashtra excise policy changes adversely impacted performance, particularly McDowell's. In Q1 F26, organic net sales grew 11.1% despite the impact of adverse policy changes in the state of Maharashtra.

**Foreign exchange**


At the CMD, we said that for full year fiscal 27 using the hedged rates already in place and for other exposures spot rates as at 31 July 2026 (including $1=£0.74 and $1=€0.87) would result in a broadly neutral foreign exchange impact on net sales and a c.$20m unfavourable impact on operating profit.


**F26 restatement of regional disclosures**


Prior year comparatives reflect the restated regional reporting structure.


Regional reported net sales may not cast exactly due to rounding. Group reported net sales are unchanged from previously reported figures. Fiscal 26 organic growth rates unrounded and adjusted for all completed acquisitions and disposals to 30 June 2026. Please see notes on disposals above.

**About Diageo** ****


Diageo is a global leader in beverage alcohol with an outstanding collection of brands across spirits and beer categories. These brands include Johnnie Walker, Crown Royal, JεB and Buchanan's whiskies, Smirnoff and Ketel One vodkas, Captain Morgan, Baileys, Don Julio, Tanqueray and Guinness.


Diageo is a global company, and our products are sold in nearly 180 countries around the world. The company is listed on both the London Stock Exchange (DGE) and the New York Stock Exchange (DEO). For more information about Diageo, our people, our brands, and performance, visit us at www.diageo.com. Visit Diageo’s global responsible drinking resource,[www.DRINKiQ.com](http://www.drinkiq.com/) for information, initiatives, and ways to share best practice.
